title: Switch the status of the favorite button
goal: Use CSS classes to change the appearance of favorite buttons while updating the press state for assistive technologies to read.
summary: classList.toggle can add or remove a class name and return whether the class name exists after the operation. Write the result to aria-pressed, and the button's appearance and pressed state can be updated together.
tasks: Add click monitoring to #save-resource in script.js. Toggles the button's is-saved class on each click, adding it the first time and removing it the second time.
Set aria-pressed to true when the is-saved class is present, and set it to false when removed. Observe whether the green background switches together with the collection status.
hint: Receive the return value of toggle in the click callback, and then use setAttribute to write aria-pressed. Click twice in succession to check whether the initial state can be restored.

example.note: Note-taking tool uses the top button to switch states. CSS changes the appearance of the button based on is-pinned, and aria-pressed records whether it is pinned.
